questions.questionText: A company places a certain amount of money into a special alternating investment scheme. For the first three years, the money earns simple interest, and for the next three years, it earns compound interest, and this pattern continues every three years. The simple interest rate is such that the investment doubles in 6 years, and the compound interest rate is also such that the investment doubles in 6 years. If the company continues this alternating pattern, starting with simple interest, after how many whole years will the investment become 4.5 times the original amount?

The average weight of a mother and her three children is 40 kg. If the weights of all three children are in A.P. with a difference of 4 kg and the mother's weight is 20 kg more than the heaviest child's weight, what is the mother's weight?
If the equations <inlineMath>{7^x} - {5^y} = 1182</inlineMath> and <inlineMath>{7^{x - 1}} + {5^{y + 1}} = 80526</inlineMath> hold true, then find the value of <inlineMath>x + y</inlineMath>.

Three friends, Aarav, Bhaskar, and Ramesh, earn money in the ratio ⁠<inlineMath>12:9:7⁠</inlineMath> and spend it in the ratio ⁠<inlineMath>15:9:8⁠</inlineMath>. If Aarav manages to save 25% of his earnings, what is the ratio of their respective savings?

In a book club of 207 members in Hyderabad, readers enjoy four different genres: Fiction, Non-Fiction, Mystery, and Fantasy. Some members do not read any of these genres. It is known that for every member who reads at least n genres, there are twice as many members who read at least <inlineMath>n - 1</inlineMath> genres, for <inlineMath>n = 2,\;3</inlineMath> and 4. If the number of members who read all four genres is equal to the number of members who read none of the genres, how many members read exactly 2 genres?

John sold two items for a total of Rs 48,000. By selling one item at a profit of 25% and the other at a loss of 15%, he ensures that the transaction ends with no overall profit or loss. Find the difference between the selling prices of the two items.

A boat covers a distance of 600 km in downstream direction. Sunday is an off day. On Monday it covers 20% of the total downstream distance. The upstream distance covered is half of the downstream distance. On Tuesdaythe boat covers 10% of the total downstream distance. The upstream distance covered is two third of the downstream distance. The ratio of downstream and upstream distance on Wednesday is 3:1 and 12% of the total downstream distance was covered.  Rest of the distance covered on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday are 24%, 18% and 16% respectively. The total upstream distance covered is 1.5times of the distance covered on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday together. The boat maintained a constant upstream speed of 10km/hr throughout the week whereas from Monday to Saturday the downstream speed varied as 20 km/hr, 12 km/hr, 18km/hr, 16km/hr, 12km/hr, 16km/hr respectively. 

Determine the ratio of the total time taken by the boat while covering upstream distance and downstream distance?

The average age of the 10 members of a city council was 46 years. On the same day, one member aged 51 stepped down from the council, and another member unfortunately passed away. A new member aged 32 was appointed to the council. Exactly one year later, in the same month, the average age of the all council members was found to be 44 years. What was the age of the member who passed away?

A gym had a certain number of members enrolled in the year 2022. In 2023, the total number of members reduced by 20% compared to 2022. Out of the members in 2023, 80% were charged a membership fee that was 20% lower than the average fee in 2022, while the remaining 20% were charged 30% more than the average 2022 fee.
What was the absolute percentage change in the total membership fee collected by the gym in 2023 compared to 2022?

A digital lock manufacturer assigns two-digit security codes using distinct digits from 0 to 9, with the condition that the first digit must not be zero. Since the codes are often printed on small devices that might be accidentally flipped upside down, certain combinations could be misread—for example, the code 86 might look like 98 when inverted. To ensure clarity and prevent such misunderstandings, how many unique two-digit codes can be assigned that are not confusing when viewed upside down?

Aman and Bharat, two chefs, are preparing fruit bowls for a food festival. Each of them has a certain number of apples and mangoes. The ratio of apples Aman has to the apples Bharat has is the same as the ratio of mangoes Bharat has to the mangoes Aman has. Interestingly, when they count their fruits, Aman discovers he has exactly one more fruit than Bharat in total. What is the smallest possible number of fruits they could have together?

Initially, a student's daily expenses amount to 75% of his allowance. After receiving a 20% increase in his allowance he chooses to spend 10% more. After all these changes, how much more has the student saved?

In 2022, the hotel chain introduced a loyalty program only for domestic guests, offering a 10% discount on the average tariff. Assuming only 50% of domestic guests enrolled and each city had 100 rooms available throughout the year in which city was the total revenue loss due to this discount the highest?

(Revenue loss = No. of discounted domestic guests × Discount per room × Occupancy × 365 ÷ 100)

Also in 2020 the hotel chain offered a business-class package exclusively to international guests priced at 1.5 times the average tariff. However only 40% of international guests opted for this package and the rest paid the standard tariff.

A truck is moving along a straight road at a constant speed of 15 m/s. A car starts from rest, 250 meters behind the truck, and accelerates at a constant rate of 2 m/s².

Will the car be able to catch up with the truck? Explain your reasoning.

If the car will catch up, estimate how long it will take for the car to reach the truck.

The truck is moving at a constant speed, so its position at any given time t is given by:

Distance of truck=v⋅t 

where:

  • v is the speed of the truck (15 m/s).
  • t is the time in seconds.

The car starts from rest and accelerates at a constant rate, so its position at any time can be expressed using the equation for uniformly accelerated motion:

⁠<inlineMath>{s_{car}} = \frac{1}{2}a{t^2}⁠</inlineMath> 

where:

scar​ = position (distance travelled) of the car at time t

a = acceleration of the car (2 m/s²)

t = time elapsed

Eight individuals, Namit, Sameer, Divan, Ashi, Neel, Ritik, Robin, and Geeta, each went on a picnic in one of the four months: September, October, November, or December. The dates available for the picnic in each month were either the 10th or the 20th, and only one person went on a picnic on any given date. Each person also visited a different destination: Manali, Udaipur, Almora, Jaisalmer, Dholavira, Nainital, Puri, or Rishikesh but not in that order. 
  • Namit’s picnic took place in October.
  • There was exactly one person between Namit and the individual who visited Puri. The Puri trip did not happen in September.
  • One person went for picnic between the ones who went to Puri and Nainital. 
  • There are five people between Sameer and Ritik, with Ritik going after Sameer. Ritik was not the last to go on a picnic.
  • Ashi went on a picnic before Robin, and both of them travelled in the same month.
  • No one went for picnic before the one who went to Almora.
  • The number of people who went before Neel equals the number of people who went after the person who visited Puri.
  • No one went for picnic between Namit and the one who went to Udaipur. Divan didn’t visit Udaipur.
  • Divan went on a picnic before Geeta, but not immediately before Geeta.
  • The number of people between Geeta, who visited Dholavira, and the person who went to Jaisalmer is four. Also, Geeta went after the one went on Jaisalmer trip.
  • Among those who went in November, one person visited Manali.
How many person (s) went to picnic after Robin?

In a partnership, two partners A and B contribute to a business with different amounts of money. The table below shows the contributions made by both partners over the first four years of the partnership

The profit for each year is distributed between the partners based on their contribution ratio.
 

In the year 2023, if Partner A wants to withdraw ₹20,000 from the business, what will be the effect on the profit-sharing ratio for that year?

options.text: Partner A’s share of the profit decreases, and Partner B’s share increases.
The profit-sharing ratio remains the same as Partner A’s contribution is only reduced by ₹20,000.
The profit-sharing ratio will change, and Partner A’s share of the profit will decrease by ₹4,000, while Partner B’s share will increase by ₹4,000.
The total profit to be distributed will decrease by ₹20,000.

questions.questionText:
The following graph shows the percentage of the total journey covered by three trucks — A, B, and C — across three terrains: City (T1), Highway (T2), and Hilly (T3). Each truck travels a certain percentage in each terrain such that the total is 100%

The second graph shows the fuel efficiency (in km/l) of each truck in each terrain:

A new Truck D travels 1200 km across terrains T1 (City) and T2 (Highway) in the ratio 1:2. Its city mileage is 20% less than Truck B’s in T1, and its highway mileage is 25% more than Truck A’s in T2. Fuel costs ₹100/litre and Truck D’s maintenance cost is ₹2/km. Truck C, for the same 1200 km journey, travels on each terrain as given in the first graph with mileage as given and maintenance cost ₹1.5/km.

Which truck has a lower total operating cost in between truck C and truck D, and what is the total fuel consumed by Truck D?

A transport department is issuing vehicle number plates in the format:
Two letters followed by four digits (e.g., AB1234).
Conditions:
  • The letters must be from the set {A, B, C, D, E}, with no repetition.
  • The digits must be from 0 to 9, and repetition is allowed.
  • The number plate must not begin with the digit 0.
  • The sum of the first two digits must be even.
If all number plates that have the same digit repeated twice consecutively in the 4-digit part are rejected, how many valid plates remain?

Eight trekkers, Ishaan, Jai, Kunal, Laksh, Mihir, Neel, Omkar, and Pranav, were standing at different locations in a forest clearing, facing various directions. Each carried a backpack of a different weight: 4kg, 6kg, 9kg, 11kg, 13kg, 17kg, and 20kg, but not necessarily in that order. However, two of them carried backpacks of the same weight.
  • Ishaan is 120 meters west of Mihir and is carrying a 13kg backpack.
  • Only Kunal is carrying the heaviest backpack, and he stands 150 meters west of the trekker whose backpack weighs 17kg.
  • Jai is 80 meters north of Pranav, who is carrying a 4kg backpack.
  • Pranav is located 200 meters south-west of Mihir.
  • Mihir and the trekker who stands 150 meters west of Kunal are carrying backpacks of the same weight.
  • Omkar stands 150 meters west of the trekker with a 9kg backpack.
  • The trekker with the third lightest backpack is 160 meters north of Kunal.
  • Laksh is not standing north-west of Ishaan.
  • Mihir’s backpack is heavier than 9kg.
  • Jai is carrying a heavier backpack than Ishaan.
  • Ishaan, Jai, and Pranav are standing in a straight vertical line.

How many trekkers are carrying heavier backpacks than the one who is standing exactly to the east of Ishaan?

Four friends A, B, C, and D are given a task carry a flag from place P to following the path instructed.
  • A starts from point P facing West. He walks 16 meters, turns right, walks 6 meters, and reaches point Q.
  • B starts at point R, which is 6 meters to the West of point Q. He walks 6 meters East, picks up the flag from A, turns left, walks 6 meters, and then turns right and walks 8 meters to reach point S.
  • At S, C is standing facing South. He takes the flag from B and walks 6 meters and root the flag at the pole there at T.
  • D is at point U which is the final destination for the flag. D walks to point T and then returns to U.
 
How much minimum distance D has to walk to get the flag from T to U, if he was initially facing South-West and turn 180 degrees after picking up the flag to walk to point U?

Jaipur, popularly known as the Pink City, stands as a vibrant symbol of India's rich architectural and cultural legacy. Established in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, the city was carefully planned with wide streets and a grid-based layout rare for its time. Its distinctive pink hue, adopted in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales, symbolises hospitality and has since become an enduring identity of the city. Jaipur is home to iconic structures like the Hawa Mahal, City Palace, Jantar Mantar (a UNESCO World Heritage site), and Amber Fort, which reflect a harmonious blend of Rajput and Mughal architectural styles. Beyond its buildings, Jaipur's living heritage is evident in its traditional crafts, local cuisine, folk music, and vibrant festivals, all of which preserve and celebrate Rajasthani culture. Today, the Pink City remains not just a tourist destination but a dynamic cultural hub where history and modernity coexist.

Which of the following best summarises the central message of the passage?

options.text: Jaipur was named the Pink City because of a royal visit in 1876 and remains a popular tourist attraction.
The Pink City is known for its ancient temples, bustling markets, and modern infrastructure.
Jaipur, with its planned design, iconic architecture, and living traditions, represents a rich blend of heritage and culture.
Jaipur’s history is limited to royal contributions and Mughal architecture.

questions.questionText:
In recent news, a major cybersecurity firm reported a critical vulnerability in widely used email encryption software. The flaw, identified in early 2024, allows hackers to intercept and decrypt sensitive communications. The company has urged users to update their software immediately to patch the issue. Additionally, experts have highlighted the importance of adopting multi-factor authentication (MFA) to safeguard accounts. The incident underscores the growing necessity for proactive cybersecurity measures to combat evolving digital threats.

Identify the error and select the correct usage based on the passage.

options.text:
Error: The phrase “to combat evolving digital threats” is redundant.
Correct Usage: “To address digital threats.”

Error: The word “decrypt” should be replaced with “encrypt” to reflect correct usage.
Correct Usage: “Allows hackers to intercept and encrypt sensitive communications.”

Error: The phrase “highlighted the importance of adopting multi-factor authentication” is vague.
Correct Usage: “Highlighted the necessity of mandatory multi-factor authentication.”
Error: No error in the passage; it is correct as written.

questions.questionText:
While anxiety is becoming more common among young people, it’s comforting to see that awareness and positivity are also growing. Schools are now introducing mental health programs, encouraging open conversations, and teaching healthy ways to cope. More and more young people are learning how to understand their emotions, ask for help, and build resilience. Even social media, which was often seen as a source of stress, is starting to create spaces that promote mental well-being and self-awareness. With the support of families, caring teachers, and accessible mental health resources, today’s youth have more chances than ever to manage anxiety and grow both emotionally and academically. The future looks hopeful for a generation that is learning to put mental health first and build lasting inner strength.

After reading the passage, select the correct tone of the same.

Launched in 2015 by the Government of India, the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (BBBP) campaign aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote the education and empowerment of girls. Rooted in growing concerns over gender discrimination and female foeticide, the initiative seeks to create awareness at the grassroots level and improve girls’ access to education. Through joint efforts by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the Ministry of Education, the program integrates advocacy, enforcement of legal measures, and local community involvement.

While the campaign has received praise for spotlighting gender inequality, critics argue that implementation gaps and insufficient funding limit its long-term impact. Nonetheless, BBBP remains a symbolic and strategic effort toward a more inclusive and gender-equal society.

Which of the following best supports the objectives of the 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' initiative?

options.text: Encouraging early marriage to protect girls from urban risks.
Promoting gender-sensitive education and community awareness programs.
Limiting girls’ access to co-educational institutions.
Offering incentives only to families with male children.

questions.questionText:
The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 marked a pivotal moment in world history, symbolising the end of decades of Cold War tensions between the Soviet bloc and the West. The Wall had stood since 1961, physically and ideologically dividing East and West Berlin, and, by extension, Germany and Europe. Its demolition was not merely the result of an overnight political shift, but a culmination of years of growing dissatisfaction within Eastern Bloc countries, coupled with changing political climates in both the Soviet Union and across Europe. Economic struggles, internal resistance movements, and a shift in Soviet policy under Mikhail Gorbachev’s reforms (such as glasnost and perestroika) played significant roles in eroding the strength of the Soviet-controlled Eastern Europe.

On November 9, 1989, East German authorities, overwhelmed by mounting pressure from the population and international developments, announced that citizens could cross the border freely. This announcement was immediately followed by joyous celebrations, with masses of East and West Germans tearing down the Wall that had separated families, ideologies, and economies for nearly three decades. The fall of the Berlin Wall didn’t just signify the end of physical barriers; it marked the beginning of the reunification of Germany and a significant step towards the eventual collapse of the Soviet Union.

The event dramatically altered the political landscape of Europe, symbolising the triumph of democratic ideals over authoritarianism. However, it also set in motion a complex set of challenges. The unification of Germany posed economic, social, and political challenges, as the integration of East Germany's weaker economy and different social structures into the more prosperous West required significant effort and resources. Furthermore, the collapse of the Eastern bloc led to the emergence of new geopolitical tensions and power dynamics in the post-Cold War world.

Which of the following statements best reflects a higher-order inference of the core ideas as described in the passage?

options.text: The fall of the Berlin Wall was primarily caused by the economic collapse of the Soviet Union, leading to the immediate reunification of Germany.
The dismantling of the Berlin Wall resulted in a straightforward unification process, but also introduced unforeseen geopolitical tensions and challenges in integrating East and West Germany.
The Berlin Wall's fall was the direct consequence of decades of Soviet authoritarian control, with little influence from internal movements within the Eastern Bloc.
The end of the Berlin Wall was a key moment in European history, representing the broader collapse of communist regimes across Eastern Europe.

questions.questionText:
India is a land of huge diversity, meditated in its languages, religions, cultures, and traditions. From the snow-capped mountains of the north to the tropical coasts of the south, every place offers a completely unique identification shaped with the aid of centuries of history. The coexistence of different faiths, fairs, cuisines, and customs highlights the country’s inclusive spirit and rich cultural fabric. 

Despite differences, this immense diversity is frequently visible as a source of solidarity, where mutual respect and shared values enhance countrywide identity. India’s variety isn't always just a characteristic; it is its greatest strength and pride. 

What is the tone of the passage above?

The syringe, a crucial medical tool, revolutionized healthcare by enabling precise drug administration and life-saving vaccinations. The earliest forms of syringes date back to ancient civilizations, but the modern hypodermic syringe was developed and introduced in the 19th century by Alexander Wood and Charles Pravaz. This invention allowed for direct injection into the bloodstream, enhancing the effectiveness of medications and pain management. Supporters argue that syringes have significantly improved public health, reduced the spread of diseases through immunization and enabled quick medical interventions. However, critics highlight concerns such as the risks of needle contamination, improper disposal leading to environmental hazards, and the rise of drug abuse facilitated by injectable substances. Despite these concerns, syringes remain indispensable in modern medicine, with ongoing innovations focusing on safer and more sustainable designs.

As per the passage, which of the following statements supports the positive impact of syringes?

options.text: Needle contamination poses risks of infections and disease transmission.
The improper disposal of syringes contributes to environmental pollution.
The rise of injectable drug abuse is linked to syringe availability.
Syringes allow direct drug administration, improving treatment efficiency.

questions.questionText:
India is home to a rich and diverse cultural heritage, with each state having its unique art forms. These art forms reflect the history, traditions, and values of the regions from which they originate. For example, Kalamkari painting from Andhra Pradesh uses natural dyes to create intricate designs often inspired by mythological themes. In Rajasthan, the miniature painting tradition is known for its detailed depictions of royal life and vibrant colours. Moving to the south, Kathakali from Kerala is a classical dance-drama that combines vibrant costumes, intricate hand gestures, and facial expressions to tell stories of Hindu mythology. 

In the northeastern state of Manipur, Raas Leela, a traditional dance, portrays the love story of Radha and Krishna. In Punjab, the folk-art form of Bhangra music and dance is known for its energetic beats and rhythmic movements that celebrate the harvest and the community. Each of these art forms not only serves as an expression of regional identity but also preserves the cultural traditions passed down through generations.

Based on the passage, which of the following conclusions can best be drawn about the relationship between art and culture in India?

options.text: The art forms of India are all rooted in historical events and do not vary significantly from one state to another.
Art forms in India are primarily a means of entertaining the masses and are not closely connected to regional traditions or values.
Each state's art forms are unique and serve as a reflection of the local culture, history, and values, helping preserve regional identities.
Indian art forms, although diverse, are mostly influenced by Western styles and are disconnected from traditional cultural practices.

questions.questionText:
Passage:

The Maha Kumbh Mela stands as a testimony to the religious dedication and cultural solidarity of India. Held once every 12 years at one among four sacred riverbanks: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik; this gigantic build-up attracts thousands and thousands of devotees, sadhus, and seekers from across the world. The occasion is rooted in an ancient legend where gods and demons fought over the pot of amrita, the nectar of immortality, spilling drops at these very locations.
The air buzzes with chants, the scent of incense swirls, and the rivers come alive as pilgrims immerse themselves within the holy waters, believing it purifies their souls and frees them from the cycle of rebirth. Beyond its religious significance, the Maha Kumbh reflects a colourful, undying tapestry of religion, resilience, and human connection; a dwelling bridge between fantasy and fact.

What is the tone of the passage?

Philosophers have offered diverse and often conflicting views on the nature of poverty and wealth. For some, excessive wealth and poverty both threaten social harmony, as they lead to division and unrest. They advocated for a balanced society where resources are more evenly distributed. Similarly, every Christian thinker emphasised the moral responsibility of the wealthy to care for the poor, viewing wealth as a potential distraction from spiritual virtue.

On the other hand, philosophers like Ayn Rand argued that wealth, when earned through individual effort and innovation, is a sign of personal excellence and should not be vilified. In this view, poverty is not necessarily a social injustice but can result from personal choices or lack of ambition.

Which of the following best summarises the tone and main idea of the passage?

options.text: Balances moral and individual views on poverty and wealth.
Explores philosophical tensions between ethical duty and personal achievement regarding wealth.
Focuses only on religious views of poverty.

questions.questionText:
Passage:

Education is now not a one-size-fits-all. Personalised studying, an approach tailored to male or female college students' strengths, wishes, and pastimes, is reshaping classrooms around the world. With the assistance of technology, teachers can now track each student’s progress in real time, imparting focused lessons and resources to close gaps or address challenges wherein needed. Adaptive knowledge platforms regulate content material based on a pupil’s performance, ensuring they learn at their own pace.

This method empowers college students to take ownership of their studying journey, fostering independence and motivation. For example, a scholar struggling with maths would possibly receive interactive tutorials. Personalised teaching also supports various learning styles; visual learners can discover movies, auditory learners can interact with podcasts, and hands-on inexperienced persons can address practical responsibilities.

Which of the following best summarises the passage on personalised learning?

options.text: Personalised learning relies entirely on technology to replace traditional teaching, making education faster and more efficient for all students.
Personalised learning tailors education to each student’s strengths and needs, using technology and flexible strategies to promote independent, diverse, and effective learning experiences.
Personalised learning focuses on helping struggling students catch up, though it may neglect those who are already performing well.
Personalised learning is a temporary trend that creates more challenges for teachers than benefits for students.

questions.questionText:
The ancient event of Samudra Manthan, or the Churning of the Ocean, symbolises a deeper philosophical truth of human life. According to it, gods and demons collaborated to churn the cosmic ocean to attain the nectar of immortality. However, before the nectar emerged, the ocean first released a deadly poison. Lord Shiva selflessly absorbed the poison to save others, turning his throat blue, earning him the name Neelkanth.

Philosophically, it was a journey of life and self-awareness. The ocean represents the thoughts, and the churning symbolises the struggles amongst good and evil inside ourselves. The poison signifies the unavoidable struggle one needs to go through before attaining enlightenment, symbolised by the nectar. Shiva’s act embodies the concept that self-sacrifice and internal strength are crucial to overcome adversity. Thus, the myth illustrates that profound rewards, like information or liberation, emerge only after enduring difficulty and chaotic events.

In light of the above, which of the following best represents the cause-and-effect relationship derived from the philosophical interpretation in the passage?

options.text: The ocean produced poison first because the gods and demons lacked unity in their efforts.
Shiva consumed the poison to assert his superiority over both gods and demons.
The emergence of poison before nectar symbolises that hardship and suffering often precede wisdom and enlightenment
The gods and demons churned the ocean to create chaos and test Shiva’s strength.

questions.questionText:
Ethics is frequently seen as a machine of right and wrong, however, psychology indicates that our moral selections are hardly ever merely logical. Instead, they are shaped by emotions, upbringing, social surroundings, and even unconscious biases. People don’t usually comply with moral regulations due to the fact that they understand them; they frequently follow them because they experience remorse while breaking them, or because society rewards certain behaviours. 

Psychologists argue that ethics isn't always only a philosophical idea, but a set of behaviours shaped by cultural values and mental patterns. What’s visible as moral in one society can be judged in a different way in every other. This doesn’t suggest that ethics are meaningless; however, it suggests that information about how human beings behave is essential to constructing a genuinely moral society.
 

Which of the following best summarises the central idea of the passage?

options.text: Ethical behaviour is mostly taught through childhood rules and rarely changes later in life.
Ethical decisions are influenced by personal emotions, social settings, and cultural values, not just logic or universal rules.
Ethics is a fixed set of principles agreed upon by all societies and enforced by psychological pressure.
People follow ethics only because they fear punishment or judgment by others in society.

questions.questionText:
The psychological development of the human brain unfolds in phases, marked by biological milestones and cognitive shifts. In early childhood, the brain’s neuroplasticity the ability to reorganize itself by forming new neural connections is at its highest. This enables children to rapidly absorb language, develop basic reasoning, and form emotional attachments, all influenced significantly by external stimuli such as social interaction, nurturing, and play. However, this malleability is also a vulnerability; adverse experiences or neglect during this phase can cause enduring developmental delays or behavioural disorders.
Adolescence introduces a new cognitive paradox. The limbic system, which governs emotion, develops earlier than the prefrontal cortex, responsible for judgment and self-regulation. This temporal mismatch explains the risk-prone behaviour and emotional volatility observed in teenagers. Yet, it also represents a window of opportunity for value formation, ethical reasoning, and identity development, especially when adolescents are exposed to challenging ideas and diverse environments.
In adulthood, while the brain’s structural changes slow, its psychological evolution continues. Adults often rely more on experiential learning and reflective thinking, shaped by cultural exposure, personal setbacks, and social bonds. Contrary to outdated beliefs, the adult brain does not become static; rather, it refines, integrates, and even reinterprets earlier beliefs based on lived experience. Mental flexibility, lifelong learning, and emotional resilience play a larger role in sustaining psychological maturity than age alone.
Modern neuroscience suggests that brain development is not linear but recursive early experiences influence later development, but later insights can also reframe past traumas or gaps. Thus, psychological growth is not simply about crossing developmental milestones but about how individuals continuously engage with life cognitively, emotionally, and socially.
Which of the following inferences can be most reasonably drawn from the passage as a whole?

options.text: While early childhood provides the optimal environment for neurological growth due to heightened neuroplasticity, the brain’s developmental trajectory becomes increasingly rigid and biologically predetermined as individuals transition into adolescence and adulthood, leaving little room for cognitive or emotional transformation.

Although adolescence is characterized by emotional instability due to neurological asynchrony, it is the only period in life when moral reasoning and identity formation are significantly influenced by external experiences, rendering later-life changes less impactful or meaningful.

The psychological development of the human brain is an evolving, lifelong process shaped not only by biological phases but also by experiential learning, emotional interactions, and reflective thinking, suggesting that individuals can adapt, reinterpret, and grow cognitively and emotionally across all stages of life.

Neuroscientific evidence confirms that cognitive and emotional development are compartmentalized in distinct life phases, each governed by specific brain structures and resistant to influence from earlier or later experiences, thus implying a linear and irreversible growth model.

questions.questionText:
Globalisation has not only accelerated economic integration but has also deeply influenced cultural identities across the world. As global media, fashion, food, and entertainment become more accessible, traditional customs and local values often blend with or give way to global norms. This cultural exchange has created new forms of identity hybrid in nature where individuals navigate both global trends and indigenous traditions.

While globalisation promotes cross-cultural understanding and appreciation, it can also dilute local heritage. Languages, rituals, and community—practices that once thrived in isolation—now face marginalisation as global culture becomes dominant. For instance, younger generations may adopt international lifestyles that differ from their ancestral roots, creating generational divides and reshaping community cohesion.

Thus, the cultural impact of globalisation is layered: it encourages diversity and dialogue but also raises concerns about the erosion of unique cultural footprints. The challenge lies in balancing global participation with the preservation of local identity.

Which of the following best reflects a nuanced cause-and-effect relationship presented in the passage?

options.text: The prevalence of global consumerism inherently undermines the legitimacy of traditional belief systems.
The merging of international media and local culture fosters complex identities shaped by both heritage and modernity.
The introduction of foreign cultural products ensures the extinction of indigenous practices over successive generations.
Generational divides emerge solely due to linguistic shifts resulting from globalisation.

questions.questionText:
Economic activities form the foundation of any nation's development, reflecting how resources are utilised to generate value. These activities classified as primary, secondary, and tertiary operate in an interdependent manner. While primary activities ensure resource availability, secondary activities add value through processing, and tertiary services support both by facilitating operations and enhancing efficiency.
Their influence on the economy is not merely quantitative, such as contributions to GDP, but also qualitative, shaping employment patterns, infrastructure development, and technological innovation. Economies that diversify their activities across all three sectors tend to be more resilient and adaptive to global changes. For example, over-reliance on one sector may make a nation vulnerable to external shocks, whereas a balanced structure enables smoother economic transitions and sustainable growth.
Which of the following best summarises the central idea of the passage?

options.text: A country’s economic strength is solely determined by how much it exports or produces through manufacturing.
Diversification and balanced integration of all types of economic activities contribute to a nation’s long-term economic resilience and adaptability.
Economic activities are independent efforts that impact only short-term national income levels.
Primary activities are the most significant since they provide the basic resources for all other sectors.

questions.questionText:
Behind every purchase we make, there’s more going on than just comparing prices or features. People often believe they choose products based on logic and practical reasons, but research in psychology shows otherwise. Our emotions, hidden thoughts, and the way people around us behave can strongly influence what we decide to buy, even if we’re not aware of it.

Marketers understand this very well and use it to their advantage. For example, they might create a sense of urgency by saying something is “limited time only” or show that many others are buying the product to make it seem more trustworthy. Even small things like the way a store is arranged or the colour of packaging can affect our decisions without us realising it. In addition, personal experiences, cultural background, and even our mood at the moment can quietly shape our preferences.
   
Which of the following best illustrates the cause-and-effect relationship presented in the passage?

options.text: Consumers buy products after conducting a purely logical analysis of price and features.
Emotional triggers, subconscious biases, and social cues cause consumers to make decisions that may not be based on rational evaluation.
Marketing techniques are ineffective because most buyers are immune to psychological influence.
Past experiences and mood are irrelevant to consumer choices, which are driven mainly by need and affordability.

questions.questionText:
The internet has revolutionised how the younger era learns, communicates, and perceives. While it gives instantaneous access to data and international connectivity, it also subtly shapes intellectual and emotional improvement. Prolonged screen time, social media comparisons, and the steady pressure to remain visible online have brought about growing ranges of anxiety, reduced attention spans, and identity issues among teenagers. 

At the same time, the net empowers self-expression and mastering opportunities, making it a double-edged sword. The psychological results are often complex, supplying both empowerment and emotional vulnerability depending on how the internet is used.

What can be inferred about the psychological impact of the internet on youth based on the passage?

options.text: The internet’s role in youth development is contradictory, promoting growth while potentially destabilising emotional well-being.
The internet’s cognitive benefits significantly outweigh its emotional consequences for young users.
Psychological issues in youth are more influenced by parental control than by online behaviour.
Limiting access to the internet is the most effective way to ensure stable emotional development in adolescents.

questions.questionText:
Indian literature is one of the richest and most diverse literary traditions in the world, spanning thousands of years and multiple languages. From the ancient Vedas, Upanishads, and epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana to modern works in English, Hindi, and regional languages, Indian literature has evolved while preserving its deep philosophical and cultural roots. Medieval literature saw the rise of Bhakti and Sufi poetry, emphasizing devotion and spirituality, while the colonial era brought forth progressive writers who addressed themes of freedom, social justice, and reform. In contemporary times, Indian authors such as Rabindranath Tagore, R.K. Narayan, Arundhati Roy, and Salman Rushdie have gained international recognition, blending traditional storytelling with modern themes. Indian literature continues to be a dynamic force, reflecting the country's evolving identity, struggles, and aspirations.

In light of the above, which of the following statements best summarises the passage?

options.text: Indian literature has evolved from ancient texts to modern works, reflecting cultural and historical changes.
Indian literature has remained unchanged over time, focusing only on ancient traditions.
Indian literature is limited to religious and spiritual themes without addressing social or political issues.
Indian literature primarily consists of epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana, with little influence of modern writers.

questions.questionText:
Evaporation is the process by which liquid water turns into vapour and enters the atmosphere. Several factors influence the rate of evaporation. One key factor is temperature; higher temperatures provide more energy for water molecules to escape into the air. Wind speed also affects evaporation; moving air removes the saturated layer of water vapour near the surface, allowing more evaporation to occur. Humidity plays a role as well when the air is already full of moisture, as evaporation slows down. Additionally, surface area matters; water spread over a larger area evaporates more quickly than in a limited space. These factors together determine how quickly water evaporates from surfaces in nature and daily life.

Which of the following statements best supports the information presented in the passage?

options.text: Evaporation occurs faster in humid conditions because moisture levels are already high.
A smaller surface area increases the rate of evaporation by concentrating heat.
Wind helps increase evaporation by removing moisture-saturated air near the surface.
Lower temperatures provide more energy for water molecules to evaporate quickly.
